title: Renting a flat: le loyer, le troisième étage
summary: Read a flat advert, ask about the rent and the bills, and say which floor with premier, deuxième, troisième.
focus: Housing words, ordinal numbers and the questions you ask when renting
content:
## Housing words

A home is **une maison** (a house), **un appartement** (a flat) or **un studio** (a one-room flat). Sharing a flat is **la colocation**; your flatmate is **le / la colocataire**.

- **Le / la propriétaire** owns the flat; **le / la locataire** rents it.
- **Louer** = to rent, both ways: **Je loue un studio à Lyon.** **Elle loue son appartement à des étudiants.**
- **Le loyer** is the monthly rent, **les charges** are the shared bills (water, heating, cleaning of the building) and **la caution** is the deposit you get back when you leave.
- **Déménager** = to move house: **Nous déménageons en mai** (nous keeps the **e**, like **nous mangeons**).
- **Meublé / meublée** = furnished: **un studio meublé**, **une chambre meublée**.

## Ordinals and floors

Add **-ième** to the number: **deux → deuxième**, **trois → troisième**, **vingt → vingtième**. A final **-e** drops: **quatre → quatrième**, **onze → onzième**. Two spellings change: **cinq → cinquième**, **neuf → neuvième**. And **vingt et un → vingt et unième**.

*First* is the exception: **premier** (m) / **première** (f): **le premier étage**, **la première rue**. Short forms: **1er**, **1re**, **2e**, **3e**. **Second / seconde** also means *second*, often when there are only two: **en seconde classe**.

Floors: **le rez-de-chaussée** is the ground floor, so **le premier étage** is one floor up (an American *second floor*). On a floor = **au**: **J'habite au troisième étage**, or just **au troisième**.

## Reading an ad and asking questions

A typical **annonce**: *Loue deux-pièces meublé, 45 m², 3e étage avec ascenseur, 850 € charges comprises.*

- **Un deux-pièces** has two main rooms (a living room + a bedroom); the kitchen and the bathroom don't count. **Un trois-pièces** has two bedrooms.
- **45 m²** is read **quarante-cinq mètres carrés**.
- **Charges comprises** = bills included in the rent.

Questions for the owner:

- **Le loyer est de combien ?** How much is the rent? **Il est de sept cents euros par mois.**
- **Les charges sont comprises ?** Are the bills included?
- **Il y a une caution ?** Is there a deposit?
- **C'est à quel étage ?** Which floor is it on?
- **L'appartement est libre quand ?** When is the flat available?

quiz.prompt: In a French building, 'le premier étage' is…
options: one floor above the ground floor
two floors above the ground floor
quiz.correct_answer: one floor above the ground floor
quiz.explanation: The ground floor is le rez-de-chaussée; counting starts above it, so le premier étage is one floor up (a British first floor, an American second floor).
hints: What is the ground floor called?

quiz.prompt: Le cabinet du dentiste est au ___ étage. (9th, in letters)
quiz.explanation: Neuf + -ième changes f to v: neuvième.

quiz.prompt: Nous avons trouvé un trois-pièces : nous ___ le mois prochain ! (to move house)
quiz.explanation: Déménager is an -ger verb, so the nous form keeps the e before -ons: nous déménageons.

quiz.prompt: « Le loyer est de six cent cinquante euros par mois, charges comprises. » How much does the tenant pay each month, in euros?
quiz.explanation: Six cent cinquante = 650 (cent takes no -s because a number follows). Charges comprises: the bills are already in it.

quiz.prompt: 'Un deux-pièces' is a flat with two bedrooms.
quiz.explanation: False: un deux-pièces has two main rooms, usually a living room and one bedroom. The kitchen and bathroom are not counted. Two bedrooms is un trois-pièces.

quiz.prompt: Which question asks the owner whether the bills are included in the rent?
quiz.explanation: Les charges are the shared bills; comprises (included) agrees with them: feminine plural.

quiz.prompt: La ___ est l'argent que le locataire donne au propriétaire au début et qu'il récupère à la fin.
quiz.explanation: Money you pay at the start and get back when you leave is la caution, the deposit.
hints: You get it back if the flat is in good condition.

quiz.prompt: Which is the ordinal of vingt et un (21st)?
quiz.explanation: Only the number on its own uses premier. In compound numbers the last part takes -ième: vingt et unième, trente et unième.

quiz.prompt: In 'Ma sœur habite au premier', premier should be première because the sister is a woman.
quiz.explanation: False: premier agrees with the word it describes, here l'étage (m), left out: au premier (étage). Première is for feminine nouns: la première rue.
hints: Premier what? Which word is hidden?

guide.tip: Locataire and loyer both start with lo-: the locataire pays the loyer. The propriétaire is the proprietor, the owner.

concept.title: L'état des lieux
concept.markdown: When you move in, you walk through the flat with the owner and note everything: a broken tile, a stain on the wall. This is **l'état des lieux**. You do it again when you leave. If the flat is in the same state, you get **la caution** back.

conversations.title: Calling about the ad
conversations.scenario: Camille phones Monsieur Garnier about the flat in his advert.

lines.text: Il est à quel étage ?

lines.speaker: b

lines.text: Très bien. Le loyer est de combien ?

lines.speaker: b

lines.meaning: Eight hundred euros a month.

lines.text: Les charges sont comprises ?

lines.meaning: No, there are sixty euros of charges on top.

lines.text: Et l'appartement est meublé ?
lines.meaning: And is the flat furnished?

lines.speaker: b

lines.meaning: OK. Can I come and see it on Saturday?

lines.meaning: Of course. Let's meet at ten in front of the building.

bites.title: -ième for the rest
bites.rule: Add -ième: deuxième, troisième. Drop a final -e: quatrième. Two changes: cinq → cinquième, neuf → neuvième.
bites.example_meaning: She lives on the ninth floor.

bites.title: Premier, première
bites.rule: First is the exception: premier (m), première (f). Second / seconde also means second.
bites.example: C'est la première rue à gauche.
bites.example_meaning: It's the first street on the left.

bites.title: Counting floors
bites.rule: Le rez-de-chaussée = ground floor; le premier étage is one floor up. On a floor: au troisième (étage).
bites.example: J'habite au premier, juste au-dessus du café.
bites.example_meaning: I live on the first floor, just above the café.

bites.title: Ask the owner
bites.rule: Le loyer est de combien ? Les charges sont comprises ? Il y a une caution ? C'est à quel étage ?
bites.example: Le loyer est de combien, charges comprises ?
bites.example_meaning: How much is the rent, bills included?

sorts.title: Kind of home, money, or people?
sorts.why: Studio, colocation and deux-pièces are kinds of home; loyer, caution and charges are money; propriétaire and locataire are people.

sorts.title: How is the ordinal spelt?
sorts.why: Most numbers just add -ième; those ending in -e drop it; cinq adds a u and neuf turns f into v.

spots.sentence: Le studio est au cinqième étage.
spots.why: Cinq takes a u before -ième: cinquième.

spots.sentence: C'est la premier rue à droite.
spots.why: Rue is feminine: la première rue.

spots.sentence: Nous avons déménagé au neufième étage.
spots.why: Neuf turns f into v: neuvième.

spots.sentence: Le locataire est la personne qui possède l'appartement.
spots.why: The one who owns the flat is le propriétaire; the locataire rents it.

spots.sentence: Les charges sont compris dans le loyer.
spots.why: Les charges is feminine plural: comprises.

We're looking for a furnished one-bedroom flat.

realm.content:
## Se loger à Eldmark

In Highgate, adventurers rent rooms in la tour des mages. **Séla loue un studio meublé au septième étage**; Borin prefers **le rez-de-chaussée** (no stairs for a dwarf). **Le loyer est de dix pièces d'or par mois**, and the owner wants **une caution**. Floors count up with **-ième**: **deuxième, troisième…**

vocabulary.example_meaning: The rent for the tower is ten gold coins.

vocabulary.example_meaning: The innkeeper keeps a potion as a deposit.

meadowbrook.content:
## Se loger à Meadowbrook

Before the farm, Nora rented **un studio meublé au premier étage**, above la graineterie: **la propriétaire**, c'est Rosa. Now Léo is looking for **une colocation**, and the old barn could become **un deux-pièces**, with **le grenier au deuxième étage**. **Le loyer** ? A basket of strawberries!

vocabulary.example: Rosa loue un petit studio au-dessus de la graineterie.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa rents out a small studio above the seed shop.

vocabulary.example_meaning: The owner of the cabin is the mayor.

vocabulary.example_meaning: The rent for the cabin is very low.

vocabulary.example: Léo et Nora vivent en colocation à la ferme.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Léo and Nora share the farmhouse.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Nora moved to the farm in spring.

vocabulary.example: La maison de la ferme a un seul étage.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The farmhouse has only one upper floor.

vocabulary.example_meaning: The mayor rents out the old barn to the farmers.

bites.example_meaning: The attic is on the second floor.

quiz.prompt: Rosa loue la chambre juste au-dessus de la graineterie : c'est au ___ étage.
quiz.explanation: The shop is on the ground floor, so the room above it is au premier étage; premier agrees with étage (m).
hints: The shop is on the ground floor.

quiz.prompt: In 'Léo est le locataire de la cabane près de la rivière', Léo owns the cabin.
quiz.explanation: False: le locataire rents; the owner is le / la propriétaire.

rustwake.content:
## Se loger à Rustwake

Out of le Dôme, you need a roof. Marta **loue des studios dans la vieille usine**: **au rez-de-chaussée** there's dust, **au troisième étage** a view of the desert. **Le loyer est de vingt écrous par semaine**, **charges comprises** (filtered water). **La caution** ? Your scrap armour.

vocabulary.example: Marta loue des conteneurs aux fouilleurs.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta rents out containers to scavengers.

vocabulary.example_meaning: My studio in the factory has an old radio.

vocabulary.example_meaning: The rent is twenty nuts a week.

vocabulary.example_meaning: The filtered water is part of the charges.

vocabulary.example: Pour la caution, je donne mon armure de ferraille.
vocabulary.example_meaning: For the deposit, I hand over my scrap armour.
